tier_1.name: Fault-injection harness
tier_1.what: Deterministic, rule-based corruption of a chosen step, so the true culprit is known by construction
tier_1.evidence: Spikes 3 + 3b — unambiguous ground truth; v1 was self-corrected by the agent and kept as a finding

tier_1.name: Cross-architecture benchmark
tier_1.what: Ground-truth-labelled traces from CrewAI/LangGraph — frameworks absent from every prior paper's benchmark
tier_1.evidence: Partial — Spike 2 proved a CrewAI workflow maps cleanly to the graph model. Scale-up (500-1,000 traces) is FYP-2 work

tier_1.name: Culprit Agent
tier_1.what: Identifies which agent in a failed trace is responsible (Strategist-stage hypothesis)
tier_1.evidence: Spike 1 — agent accuracy 62.5-85.7% across 5 independent runs (mean 71.4%)

tier_1.name: Error Step Localization
tier_1.what: Pinpoints the exact step where the failure originated
tier_1.evidence: Spike 1 — step accuracy 0-25% across 5 runs (mean 13.2%). Honest floor: this is the hard half, and the simplified 2-stage pipeline shows it

tier_1.name: Verification Agent
tier_1.what: Evidence-grounded confirmation of a hypothesis against the real trajectory before the Arbiter commits
tier_1.evidence: Partial — the tool-grounded Investigator stage is deliberately NOT in the simplified spike-1 pipeline. Full 3-stage reproduction is FYP-1 core work

tier_1.name: Repair Agent
tier_1.what: Generates a targeted correction (prompt, tool argument, structured output, or small function)
tier_1.evidence: Spike 8 — repair_success_rate 0.667 (4/6). Both failures share one fixable interface cause (R17)

tier_1.name: Semantic Error Diagnostic
tier_1.what: Deterministic task-constraint verification catching well-formed-but-wrong outputs. Zero LLM calls; abstains and reports coverage where no checkable constraint exists
tier_1.evidence: Spike 4 — catches known-wrong values incl. a $20.00-vs-$19.75 near-miss, zero false positives

tier_1.name: Verified Automatic Repair
tier_1.what: Re-executes downstream under a controlled replay protocol and reports a measured recovery rate before any fix is trusted
tier_1.evidence: Spike 5 — corrupted trace 97.2 recovered to 108.0 (recovery_success: true)

tier_2.name: Recovery Controller
tier_2.what: Applies a verified repair and resumes from a safe checkpoint instead of restarting the whole workflow
tier_2.status: No POC yet — genuinely new mechanical work, not a rename of anything already tested
tier_2.gate: LangGraph checkpoint/resume PoC demonstrating resume-from-verified-repair-point on at least one real workflow, by Mid-1
tier_2.fallback: Re-scope to resumption via controlled replay, which Tier 1 item #8 already delivers. The loop still closes; only the mechanism changes. Recorded per §5.3

tier_2.name: Verified Repair Memory
tier_2.what: Stores successful error-to-repair patterns and retrieves them for similar future failures
tier_2.status: One real test, and it FAILED — 0 of 8 Who&When cases ever committed to memory; agent accuracy regressed 75%->50% on a 3B backbone
tier_2.gate: Re-test on a stronger backbone against the same 8 cases. Pass = at least one committed memory AND no accuracy regression vs. the memory-off run
tier_2.fallback: Ships as a memory-on/memory-off ablation study — an evaluation contribution under §4's own table, not a dropped feature

sdk_journey.title: Install
sdk_journey.detail: One pip install. No account, no cloud dependency — the backend runs in your own container (plan §13).

sdk_journey.title: Wrap your existing workflow
sdk_journey.detail: A callback/hook per framework adapter. Your agent code is not rewritten — FR5 requires the diagnosis engine consume only the normalized trace schema, so instrumenting is additive.
sdk_journey.code:
from granite import instrument

# your existing CrewAI crew, unchanged
crew = Crew(agents=[planner, researcher, writer], tasks=[...])

# one wrap -> emits the normalized trace schema
crew = instrument(crew, project="support-bot")

sdk_journey.title: Run as you normally would
sdk_journey.detail: Every execution emits a trace: agent actions, tool calls, and the reference identifiers the execution graph is built from. PII-shaped fields are redacted before storage (R16).

sdk_journey.title: Diagnoses appear in this console
sdk_journey.detail: The pipeline runs automatically on each captured trace: graph -> Semantic Error Diagnostic -> attribution -> Repair Agent -> verified replay. Results land in Runs & Diagnoses, exactly as the real spike data does today.
